A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EHR2Path and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched despite the changed title and expanded appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original MIMIC-IV next-step prediction, trajectory simulation, outcome fine-tuning, and ablation results in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds clinical plausibility, subgroup, baseline-comparison, termination-error, and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The EHR representation, three pathway-model variants, masked summarization mechanism, LOS indicator, training objectives, and fine-tuning procedures are retained. Added budget and output-parsing explanations do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MIMIC-IV, MIMIC-IV-Note, and MIMIC-IV-ED coverage and ED, hospital, and ICU tasks. The added subgroup analyses explicitly reuse existing test sets; the new comparisons and examples examine variables already covered.

E2.justification: V3 adds an evaluated DT-GPT comparison on magnesium, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation in Appendix A.3/Table 9, plus copy-forward references in qualitative rollout plots. The statistical baseline, ETHOS, MEME, and REMed comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds sensitivity/specificity, empirical plausibility checks, subgroup stratification, and an ETHOS-supported 150-lab evaluation. It also changes the stated ICU imminent-discharge input from a random time point to the first 24 hours (v2 Table 7 versus v3 Table 13). These substantially extend the evaluation design; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds rollout plausibility audits, discharge termination-error analysis, sex/age/condition-rarity analyses, treatment and renal-panel case studies, and summary-token attention inspection. These examine realism, failure modes, heterogeneity, and compression behavior beyond v2's retained horizon, LOS, and bottleneck-size analyses.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices specify single-run results with bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals. V3 adds interval-bearing result rows but reports no new seed counts, repeated-run design, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Most retained predictive scores and ablation results remain unchanged. Table 1 changes E2P-S+T's average/maximum input tokens from 1585/5744 to 1414/4313. Substantial new findings include sensitivity/specificity, DT-GPT and subgroup scores, plausibility rates, and termination errors, including 0.16 ICU mortality sensitivity for E2P-S+T and 21.8% premature discharge.

T1.justification: The hierarchical data definitions, attention-mask equation, and information-bottleneck formulation in Sections 3.1–3.2.2 are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The core representation, pathway forecasting, and summarization contributions remain. The abstract and conclusion narrow the emphasis from a scalable framework supporting clinical decision-making toward demonstrated forecasting feasibility on MIMIC-IV and potential future clinical support.

C2.justification: V3 explains that forecasts combine patient evolution with measurement/documentation behavior and do not establish clinical utility. It adds substantive interpretations of premature discharge, subgroup differences, smoothing and treatment delays, summary attention, and the contribution of broader inputs to baseline differences. Prospective validation and deployment limitations are substantially expanded.

D1.justification: V3 clarifies the shared soft 4000-token budget, character-count-based truncation, and summary tokens replacing some raw text. Appendix A.9 adds explicit label parsing, terminal-event rules, and the ED fallback guard. Backbone, training parameters, hardware, timing, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a focused contrast between EHR2Path's broad trajectory modeling and DT-GPT's three forecasting targets. Makarov et al. was already cited in v2; Section 2 and the bibliography remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and author block change, with targeted rewrites and expanded explanations in the results, limitations, and conclusion. A Broader Impact Statement and appendix subsections are added, while the main organization and most existing methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redesigned from two radar panels into three, and Tables 2–3 gain metric rows. V3 adds termination, plausibility, comparator, and subgroup tables plus LOS, multi-step, and attention figures. The original vital-sign example is redrawn with copy-forward references; the horizon plots and existing ablation tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves diagnostic transparency through class-specific outcomes, explicit discharge failures, plausibility checks, and better-qualified clinical claims. However, new subgroup reporting contains unexplained inconsistencies: Tables 10–12 give overall ED admission accuracy a 95% interval of [0.68, 0.68], versus [0.64, 0.72] in Table 2, despite stating that the same test sets and metrics are used. These weaken the added subgroup evidence and limit the overall gain.
